about: The #913 AWS session: hours and instances per part, priced by cost.py estimate with prices.json. compare.sh session runs the parts in this order. The hours come from the time model below, not from a run.

model.journeys_size_1: 10 per product: the 8 journeys, and the cold read with working sets of 100,000 and 1M users (the 1,000-user set is journey 6, admin user lookup, which also runs after a page-cache drop)
model.minutes_per_journey_detail: coarse phase: restore 3, setup grace 1, warm-up 1.1, about 5 steps of 65 s (the run stops at the first step that fails for sure), collect 1 = 11.5; fine phase: restore 3, grace 1, warm-up and 3 steps 4.3, collect 1 = 9.3; less when a coarse step fails early, more when all 8 coarse steps are clean (no fine phase then)
model.setup_detail: up and SSH 5 min, k6 on the generators, Docker and the images (or Hearth's deploy) 10 min, reading the snapshot volume once 5 min, the first restore 3 min
model.seed_detail: server only, c7i.large (#913: the size 1 server), 1M bulk users plus 1,000 login users, then the 1M-id listing (ids.js), settle and snapshot. From the local 100k seeds (12 cores) scaled to 2 vCPU: Keycloak 70-87 s, Zitadel 139 s, Ory 39 s per 100k; Hearth's 10M drill seed took 1,408 s on r7i.large. Authentik took about 20 minutes per 100k on 12 cores (blueprints, about 93 users/s with 4 processes): on 2 vCPU about 15 to 25 users/s, so 11 to 18 h, which may pass the 16 h lifetime cap (owner decision)
